World map — four art styles, three exploration states

Same geography in all twelve: Haven lower-left with three roads, the silt-black lake north-centre, the impassable mountain wall east, Thornwood forest NW, the burned Ashmark NE, Fallow Coast delta SE, Gravel Downs SW. Each style's three states were derived from its own full map, so the terrain is identical across a row. Click any image to enlarge.

A — Realistic

Satellite-and-relief rendering, true terrain textures, low afternoon sun. Fog is volumetric cloud.

Landmarks are diegetic — actual tiny buildings. Readable at full size, but a POI icon layer would have to sit on top.

B — Hand-drawn map

Aged parchment, iron-gall ink, crosshatching, watercolour wash, sea serpent. Fog is undrawn parchment.

The unexplored land isn't hidden — it was never surveyed. Strokes stop mid-line at the edge of knowledge.

C — Very cartoony

Bold outlines, chunky shapes, candy palette, oversized charming landmarks. Fog is storybook cloud.

Highest icon readability by a distance. Every POI reads at a glance, even scaled down.

D — Embroidered tapestry

Dyed wool on linen: satin-stitch rivers, french-knot forests, couched gold-thread roads. Fog is bare unwoven cloth.

The creative slot. The guild's story is literally stitched in as it's learned — and the bare cloth carries faint sketched guide-lines, which reads as rumour vs knowledge.
